A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same MOON2.0 study, and all 11 supplied pages are readable and comparable. Both end with references and contain no appendix; the supplementary materials mentioned in their text are not included in either PDF.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval, classification, and attribute-prediction experiments in Tables 1–3, component ablations in Table 4, and attention visualizations in Figure 7.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, ablations, and qualitative visualizations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical modality-driven MoE, dual-level alignment, image-text co-augmentation, and dynamic sample filtering procedures, including their objectives and representation extraction.

E1.justification: Both versions use MBE2.0, M5Product, and Fashion200K for the same retrieval and classification tasks, with attribute prediction additionally evaluated on MBE2.0.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the same nine baselines: SigLIP2, BGE-VL-Large, FashionCLIP, InternVL3-2B, Qwen2.5-VL-3B, GME, MM-Embed, CASLIE-S, and MOON. The modality-mixed-training comparisons are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 4–5.1 retain identical data splits, training settings, augmentation rules, zero-shot evaluation procedures, and metrics. MBE2.0 still contains 5,751,594 training samples and 636,241 test samples.

E4.justification: The training-mixture analysis in Figure 2, four component-removal ablations in Table 4, and attention case studies in Figure 7 are identical.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point estimates without repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 and findings in the result figures are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains MOON2.0's MBE2.0 classification accuracy of 68.08 and attribute-prediction accuracy of 84.29.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and formulations in Equations 1–11 are identical, including routing weights, alignment losses, regularization, and sample reliability. No theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain identical claims about modality balancing, the proposed components, MBE2.0, and state-of-the-art zero-shot performance.

C2.justification: Sections 5.2–5.4 retain the same explanations of performance, component contributions, and attention alignment. Applicability statements and qualifications are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility disclosures remain identical, including the learning rate, cosine scheduler, approximately 18-hour training on 64 A100 GPUs, and batch size of four per GPU. The MBE2.0 dataset access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning, citations, and all 59 reference entries are identical.

P1.justification: Only the first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 24 March 2026 to v3 dated 29 July 2026, with its hyperlink updated accordingly. The paper's wording, headings, and section structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp shifts downward and slightly right. All seven figures, four tables, captions, and body layouts are unchanged; pages 2–11 render identically.

improvement.justification: The scientific text, equations, experiments, results, references, and substantive presentation are identical. Updating and repositioning the arXiv version stamp neither improves nor harms the paper's overall quality.
